items.title: Max Weber
items.body: Max Weber worked across Economics, Sociology, History, Law, Politics.
items.lesson: Capitalism's growth is due in part to the Protestant work ethic.
items.takeaway: Snapshot the thinker, then read the wiki.
items.example: “The fate of our times is characterized by rationalization and intellectualization and, above all, by the disenchantment of the world.”

items.title: Michel de Montaigne
items.body: Michel de Montaigne worked across Skepticism.
items.lesson: Tranquillity depends upon detachment from the opinion of others.
items.takeaway: Snapshot Renaissance humanism, Renaissance skepticism, then read the wiki.
items.example: “I want to be seen here in my simple, natural, ordinary fashion, without straining or artifice; for it is myself that I portray...I am myself the matter of my book.”

items.title: Michel Foucault
items.body: Taking up some of the work begin by Nietzsche, Michel Foucault explored further what constitutes truth. Looking at specific domains such as sexuality, mental illness, and incarceration, Foucault describes how regimes of truth and discourses change over time. His work has been foundational to many social movements.
items.lesson: Concepts and words change over time; an archaeology of thought should be performed.
items.takeaway: Snapshot Post-Structuralism, then read the wiki.
items.example: “The most defenseless tenderness and the bloodiest of powers have a similar need of confession. Western man has become a confessing animal.”

items.title: Montesquieu
items.body: Montesquieu worked across Political philosophy.
items.lesson: Despotism is an ever-present danger for any government that's not already despotic.
items.takeaway: Snapshot Classical liberalism, then read the wiki.
items.example: “A man should be mourned at his birth, not at his death.”

items.title: Niccolò Machiavelli
items.body: Niccolò Machiavelli's writings have been looked to by generations of political theorists. He is also seen as an early voice advocating realpolitik. In his “Discourses on Livy,” he exposed “at times it is a very wise thing to simulate madness,” which presaged Richard Nixon’s “madman theory” of foreign policy. Many feel that the Trump Administration represents a return to madman politics.
items.lesson: The success of a nation state is paramount.
items.takeaway: Snapshot Political Realism, then read the wiki.
items.example: “Since love and fear can hardly exist together, if we must choose between them, it is far safer to be feared than loved.”

items.title: Noam Chomsky
items.body: Noam Chomsky worked across Linguistics, Politics, Media.
items.lesson: If we assume that our own government is naturally more ethical than other government, we are choosing to live in a world of comforting illusion.
items.takeaway: Snapshot Analytic philosophy, then read the wiki.
items.example: “States are violent to the extent that they're powerful, that's roughly accurate.”

items.title: Parmenides
items.body: Parmenides worked across Metaphysics, Ontology.
items.lesson: Everything has always existed; there was never a time when there was nothing.
items.takeaway: Snapshot Pre-Socratic, then read the wiki.
items.example: “Thinking and the thought that it is are the same; for you will not find thinking apart from what is, in relation to which it is uttered.”

items.title: Peter Singer
items.body: Peter Singer worked across Ethics, Bioethics, Analytic Philosophy.
items.lesson: In suffering, the animals are our equals.
items.takeaway: Snapshot Utilitarianism, then read the wiki.
items.example: “It is easy for us to criticize the prejudices of our grandfathers, from which our fathers freed themselves. It is more difficult to search for prejudices among the beliefs and values that we hold.”

items.title: Pierre-Joseph Proudhon
items.body: Pierre-Joseph Proudhon worked across Liberty, Property, Authority, Poverty, Social Justice, Egalitarianism.
items.lesson: Private ownership of land is a theft of the commons.
items.takeaway: Snapshot Socialism, Anarchism, Mutualism, then read the wiki.
items.example: “Property is robbery! That is the war-cry of '93! That is the signal of revolutions!”

items.title: Plato
items.body: Plato worked across Rhetoric, Art, Literature, Epistemology, Justice, Virtue, Politics, Education, Family, Militarism.
items.lesson: Permanent ideals (Forms) exist outside time and space; in this world, we experience only ephemeral copies (Particulars) of those ideals.
items.takeaway: Snapshot Platonism, then read the wiki.
items.example: “I shall assume that your silence gives consent”

items.title: Plotinus
items.body: Plotinus worked across Platonism, Metaphysics, Mysticism.
items.lesson: What's real is a product of thought; for something to exist it be thought.
items.takeaway: Snapshot Neoplatonism, then read the wiki.
items.example: “Perhaps, the good and the beautiful are the same, and must be investigated by one and the same process; and in like manner the base and the evil.”

items.title: Protagoras
items.body: Protagoras worked across Language, Semantics, Relativism, Rhetoric, Agnosticism, Ethics.
items.lesson: Man is the measure of all things.
items.takeaway: Snapshot Sophism, then read the wiki.
items.example: “Man is the measure of all things.”

items.title: Pythagoras
items.body: Pythagoras worked across Metaphysics, Music, Mathematics, Ethics, Politics.
items.lesson: Much of knowledge is actually a remembrance from previous lives.
items.takeaway: Snapshot Pythagoreanism, then read the wiki.
items.example: “There is geometry in the humming of the strings, there is music in the spacing of the spheres.”

items.title: Ralph Waldo Emerson
items.body: Ralph Waldo Emerson worked across Individualism, Mysticism.
items.lesson: There is a unity of nature that extends to every particle of matter.
items.takeaway: Snapshot Transcendentalism, then read the wiki.
items.example: “The stars awaken a certain reverence, because though always present, they are inaccessible; but all natural objects make a kindred impression, when the mind is open to their influence. Nature never wears a mean appearance.”

items.title: René Descartes
items.body: René Descartes worked across Metaphysics, Epistemology, Mathematics.
items.lesson: Mathematics begins with incontrovertible premises and through deduction arrives at irrefutable conclusions.
items.takeaway: Snapshot Cartesianism, then read the wiki.
items.example: “I think, therefore I am.”

items.title: Richard Rorty
items.body: Richard Rorty worked across Epistemology, Philosophy of Language, Philosophy of Mind, Ethics, Metaphilosophy, Liberalism, Meta-Epistemology.
items.lesson: There is no distinction between language and world when determining the truth of what we say.
items.takeaway: Snapshot Pragmatism, Postanalytic Philosophy, then read the wiki.
items.example: “Truth is what your contemporaries let you get away with.”

items.title: Robert Nozick
items.body: Robert Nozick worked across Political Philosophy, Ethics, Epistemology.
items.lesson: The best reason to want a libertarian society is because it respects individual rights.
items.takeaway: Snapshot Analytic, Libertarianism, then read the wiki.
items.example: “Individuals have rights and there are things no person or group may do to them (without violating their rights).”

items.title: Roger Bacon
items.body: Roger Bacon worked across Theology, Natural philosophy.
items.lesson: Mathematics, unlike other sciences, can be used to arrive at certainty.
items.takeaway: Snapshot Scholasticism, then read the wiki.
items.example: “Reasoning draws a conclusion and makes us grant the conclusion, but does not make the conclusion certain, nor does it remove doubt so that the mind may rest on the intuition of truth, unless the mind discovers it by the path of experience.”

items.title: Roland Barthes
items.body: Roland Barthes worked across Semiotics, Literary Theory, Narratology, Linguistics.
items.lesson: Semiotics and the study of signs is useful in showing the second-order signs and connotations of bourgeois cultural myths.
items.takeaway: Snapshot Semiotics, then read the wiki.
items.example: “The bourgeoisie is defined as the social class which does not want to be named.”

items.title: Rosa Luxemburg
items.body: Rosa Luxemburg worked across Political Philosophy, Economics.
items.lesson: Without elections, freedom of the press and assembly, and freedom of opinion, public institutions die.
items.takeaway: Snapshot Marxism, then read the wiki.
items.example: “Freedom only for the members of the government, only for the members of the Party — though they are quite numerous — is no freedom at all. Freedom is always the freedom of dissenters.”

items.title: Seneca
items.body: Seneca worked across Ethics.
items.lesson: It is better to live a meaningful life than a long life.
items.takeaway: Snapshot Stoicism, then read the wiki.
items.example: “It is not the man who has too little, but the man who craves more, that is poor.”

items.title: Sigmund Freud
items.body: Sigmund Freud worked across Politics, Religion, Psychology, Sociology, History.
items.lesson: There is an active unconscious part of the mind which pressures and influences how we act and behave.
items.takeaway: Snapshot Psychoanalysis, then read the wiki.
items.example: “It is easy to see that the ego is that part of the id which has been modified by the direct influence of the external world.”

items.title: Simone de Beauvoir
items.body: Simone de Beauvoir worked across Political Philosophy, Feminism, Ethics, Existential Phenomenology.
items.lesson: The Self is presumed to be male, causing women to always be defined as the Other.
items.takeaway: Snapshot Existentialism, French Feminism, Marxism, then read the wiki.
items.example: “One is not born, but rather becomes, a woman.”

items.title: Slavoj Žižek
items.body: Slavoj Žižek worked across Ideology, Marxism, Ontology, Political Theory, Psychoanalysis, Cultural Studies, Film Theory, Theology.
items.lesson: Serious questions about the nature of political power are obscured by trying to justify utopia's elusiveness
items.takeaway: Snapshot Continental Philosophy, then read the wiki.
items.example: “Lacan's definition of human deception: We deceive the Other by means of the truth itself; in a universe in which all are looking for the true face beneath the mask, the best way to lead them astray is to wear the mask of truth itself.”

items.title: Socrates
items.body: Socrates worked across Epistemology, Ethics.
items.lesson: Greater knowledge of the universe does not change human behavior.
items.takeaway: Snapshot Classical Greek, then read the wiki.
items.example: “What I do not know I do not think I know either”

items.title: Sojourner Truth
items.body: Sojourner Truth worked across Social Philosophy, Political Philosophy, Women's Rights.
items.lesson: If woman are so frail that they need special treatment, why has no one ever offered her, a black woman, the traditional gentlemanly deference due a woman.
items.takeaway: Snapshot the thinker, then read the wiki.
items.example: “That man over there says that women need to be helped into carriages, and lifted over ditches, and to have the best place everywhere. Nobody ever helps me into carriages, or over mud-puddles, or gives me any best place! And ain't I a woman?”

items.title: Søren Kierkegaard
items.body: Søren Kierkegaard worked across Christianity, Metaphysics, Epistemology, Aesthetics, Ethics, Psychology.
items.lesson: To understand the world, one has to look not at ideas but at individual entities.
items.takeaway: Snapshot Christian Existentialism, then read the wiki.
items.example: “Between these two moments lies the leap, which no science has explained and which no science will explain.”

items.title: Susan Sontag
items.body: Susan Sontag worked across Politics, Art, Feminism.
items.lesson: The convenience of modern photography has created an overabundance of visual material.
items.takeaway: Snapshot the thinker, then read the wiki.
items.example: “So successful has been the camera's role in beautifying the world that photographs, rather than the world, have become the standard of the beautiful.”

items.title: Thales of Miletus
items.body: Thales of Miletus worked across Ethics, Metaphysics, Mathematics, Astronomy.
items.lesson: Everything is composed of water just in different forms.
items.takeaway: Snapshot Naturalism, then read the wiki.
items.example: “Water is the first principle of everything.”

items.title: Theodor W. Adorno
items.body: Theodor W. Adorno was a critic of the industrialization of the production of art. This critique presaged consolidation of the media industry, which changes not only artistic works but also narrative technique and ultimately self-understanding.
items.lesson: There's no context-free thought: there is not a universal standpoint to discern “truth,” only one that has socio-historical context.
items.takeaway: Snapshot Frankfurt School, then read the wiki.
items.example: “Bourgeois society is ruled by equivalence. It makes the dissimilar comparable by reducing it to abstract quantities. To the enlightenment, that which does not reduce to numbers, and ultimately to the one, becomes illusion.”

items.title: Thomas Aquinas
items.body: Thomas Aquinas worked across Metaphysics, Logic, Theology, Mind, Epistemology, Ethics, Politics.
items.lesson: Faith is independent from reason; believe provides answers to questions that are undecidable by reason alone.
items.takeaway: Snapshot Thomism, then read the wiki.
items.example: “Reason in man is rather like God in the world.”

items.title: Thomas Hobbes
items.body: Thomas Hobbes famous for his claim that the state of nature is “a war of all against all” that required a Leviathan to establish order. Hobbes’s worldview has been referenced to justify a muscular foreign policy.
items.lesson: Matter in motion comprises the universe and nothing else; the universe is a large mechanism.
items.takeaway: Snapshot Social Contract, then read the wiki.
items.example: “The condition of man…is a condition of war of everyone against everyone.”

items.title: Thomas Kuhn
items.body: Thomas Kuhn worked across Philosophy of Science, Historiographical externalism.
items.lesson: To understand how science unfolds we must look at its history, not just logic.
items.takeaway: Snapshot Analytic, then read the wiki.
items.example: “"Normal science" means research firmly based upon one or more past scientific achievements, achievements that some particular scientific community acknowledges for a time as supplying the foundation for its further practice”

items.title: Thomas Nagel
items.body: Thomas Nagel worked across Politics, Ethics, Philosophy of Mind, Epistemology.
items.lesson: We cannot completely assume a ”view from nowhere,” that is completely abandon our subjectivity.
items.takeaway: Snapshot Analytic philosophy, then read the wiki.
items.example: “Eventually, I believe, current attempts to understand the mind by analogy with man-made computers that can perform superbly some of the same external tasks as conscious beings will be recognized as a gigantic waste of time.”

items.title: Voltaire
items.body: Voltaire worked across Politics, Religion, Historiography, Skepticism.
items.lesson: Every fact and theory in history has been revised at some point.
items.takeaway: Snapshot Deism, then read the wiki.
items.example: “Divorce is probably of nearly the same age as marriage. I believe, however, that marriage is some weeks the more ancient.”

items.title: W. E. B. Du Bois
items.body: W. E. B. Du Bois worked across Politics, Sociology, History.
items.lesson: We aspire to a broader fuller life.
items.takeaway: Snapshot the thinker, then read the wiki.
items.example: “To be a poor man is hard, but to be a poor race in a land of dollars is the very bottom of hardships.”
